crop.notes: Clipping is the whole 'Domino' sporting-notes column. Only the first item ('To Fight the Winner. "Denver" Ed Smith Will Be at the Ringside') is about Allen; the rest covers Ed Corrigan's Utah pony race, football rules, Billy Robinson's benefit, the Cincinnati ball grounds and the Oakley track. The Allen item is complete.

ocr.notes: Gist readable but many letter errors (e.g. 'Alles', 'Ailes', 'Jacksomiile'); stakes misread ('3),'00' for $5,000)

title.suggested: Tom Allen Expects Ed Smith in St. Louis on the Way to Jacksonville

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic reported that Tom Allen, who won heavily betting on Ed Smith against Joe Goddard, had a letter from Smith saying he would visit St. Louis, then go with Allen to Jacksonville to challenge the Corbett-Mitchell winner.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Saturday Morning, December 23, 1893, page 6. The challenge is Smith's, not Allen's.

facts.fact: Allen won a large sum betting on Ed Smith when Smith defeated Joe Goddard at New Orleans

Allen received a letter from Ed Smith saying Smith would stop in St. Louis for about a week and then go with Allen to Jacksonville, where Smith meant to challenge the winner of the Corbett-Mitchell fight
Allen said he wanted Smith to meet Peter Jackson and that he had seen Smith and Jackson box at Battery D, Chicago
facts.quote: I want to see Smith meet Jackson as soon as he can. I saw him meet the colored man in Battery D, Chicago, and he could have knocked him out in 10 rounds.

facts.fact: Allen said he had been receiving letters from Charley Mitchell, who said he was already in fine shape
facts.quote: I have been receiving letters from Mitchell and he says he is in fine shape already.

notes: Current title says Allen issued a challenge; it was Smith who planned to challenge. Current summary is a truncated fragment.
